# Game Loop Pattern

#### Course: Canvas Foundations

## Game Loop Pattern

The animation works. But right now the logic and the drawing are mixed together in one function. As Brick Breaker grows, with a ball, a paddle, and 30 bricks all updating at the same time, that gets messy fast.

The cleaner way is to split responsibilities into three functions.

```html
1<!DOCTYPE html>
2<html lang="en">
3    <head>
4        <meta charset="UTF-8">
5        <title>Canvas</title>
6        <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">
7    </head>
8    <body>
9        <canvas id="gameCanvas" width="400" height="300">
10        </canvas>
11        <script src="script.js">
12        </script>
13    </body>
14</html>
```

```css
1*  {
2    margin: 0;
3    padding: 0;
4    box-sizing: border-box;
5}
6body  {
7    display: flex;
8    justify-content: center;
9    align-items: center;
10    height: 100vh;
11    background: #f0f0f0;
12}
13canvas  {
14    display: block;
15    border: 1px solid #ccc;
16    background: #fff;
17}
```

```javascript
1const canvas = document.getElementById("gameCanvas");
2const ctx = canvas.getContext("2d");
3let x = 20;
4let dx = 2;
5function update()  {
6    x += dx;
7    if (x > 360 || x < 0) dx = -dx;
8}
9function draw()  {
10    ctx.clearRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height);
11    ctx.fillRect(x, 130, 40, 40);
12}
13function gameLoop()  {
14    update();
15    draw();
16    requestAnimationFrame(gameLoop);
17}
18gameLoop();
```

Click Run Code and you will see the square bouncing back and forth across the canvas.

Here, update() handles all movement and state changes - it does not touch the canvas at all. draw() only renders - it reads positions but does not change them. gameLoop() calls both in the right order and schedules the next frame. The pattern looks like this every time:

```javascriptDOM
function update() { /* move things, check collisions / } function draw()   { / clear then paint everything */  } function gameLoop() { update(); draw(); requestAnimationFrame(gameLoop); } gameLoop();
```

Keeping update() and draw() separate means you can test your movement logic without worrying about rendering, and add new visual elements to draw() without touching the physics. In Brick Breaker, this separation is what keeps the codebase readable when the paddle, ball, and brick grid are all updating in the same loop.

![Circular flowchart showing gameLoop calling update then draw then requestAnimationFrame back to gameLoop](data:application/octet-stream;base64,)
